overall.summary: All 193 claims and all prose numbers reproduce, but one sentence (and its claim C116) credits the combined-bill part with a voice-mail interaction it does not carry; the C093 threshold sentence, one worth-checking item, the part-scope day-minutes sentence in the first block and the nudge-chain text are weakened; the rest holds.

findings.statement: It also rises more for customers without voice-mail messages: from about 2% to about 11%, against about 1% to about 2% for a typical customer with messages (and so a voice-mail plan).
findings.check: probe the combined-bill part's contribution over day charge 19.07 -> 42.40 US dollars, typical customer, at 0 messages/no plan, 17 messages/plan, and 17 messages/no plan
findings.evidence: ann_89 contribution goes -0.552 -> -0.316 (+0.236) at 0 messages and -0.071 -> +0.165 (+0.236) at 17 messages: the same rise on the logit, so messages do not amplify the day-charge effect in this part. The group numbers (2.26% -> 10.55%, 1.46% -> 1.78%) are identical to C103's, which is the voice-mail-plan hinge 3460 in highDayUsageHinges (ann_88); C116's own counterfactual through this part is -0.077 against -1.39 for C103. Through ann_89 alone the typical customer would only go from about 2.3% to about 2.8%.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe <T> --hold typical --set "voice mail plan=0" --set "number vmail messages=0" --sweep "total day charge=19.07,30.69,42.4"
uv run python -m explaneat verify probe <T> --hold typical --set "voice mail plan=1" --set "number vmail messages=17" --sweep "total day charge=19.07,30.69,42.4"

findings.statement: interaction in dayEveChargeCascade: day charge raises risk more at 0 voice-mail messages (2.3% -> 10.6%) than with messages (1.5% -> 1.8%)
findings.check: as V1; compare the claim's evidence.counterfactual_did_through_part with C103
findings.evidence: numbers reproduce mechanically (recheck) but describe the voice-mail-plan hinge of ann_88, not this part: equal +0.236 logit rise in ann_89 in both groups; did through part -0.077 vs C103 -1.39

findings.statement: a higher daytime charge lowers it steadily up to about 15.64 US dollars (between 7.93 and 31.04 for different customers), then no further, from about 11% to about 2% (19.07 -> 42.40 US dollars)
findings.check: probe --claim C093; sweep day charge 8:44 for the typical customer at 3 service calls
findings.evidence: for the typical customer the part acts on, the part keeps falling until about 31-32 US dollars (ann_90 +3.21 at 8, +0.35 at 29, +0.07 from 32 on), so the fall in the sentence's own example (10.8% at 19.07, 2.8% at 42.40) happens entirely above the stated 15.64. 15.64 is the median fold across customers; the typical case sits at the top of the stated spread. The added clause in drafted.annotations.ann_90[3] ('flattening out near the bottom because the predicted chance cannot go much lower') is also off: the flattening is the hinge 5395 switching off, not saturation. Direction and the population spread are right.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe <T> --claim C093
uv run python -m explaneat verify probe <T> --hold typical --set "number customer service calls=3" --sweep "total day charge=8:44:13"

findings.statement: same C093 sentence, with 'flattening out near the bottom because the predicted chance cannot go much lower'
in the combined bill part, more voice-mail messages raise the predicted chance, while across the whole model they lower it
findings.check: probe a typical plan holder over messages 0..45; read C025's average curve
findings.evidence: the whole-model lowering is the voice-mail plan switching on with the first message (C025 is a dip, turning at 1 message; mean log-odds -2.47 at 0, -3.89 at 17, then rising to -3.15 at 36). For a plan holder, more messages raise the whole-model risk too: 0.3% at 0, 0.6% at 10, 1.1% at 20, 1.6% at 32, 2.5% at 45. The contrast the item flags is mostly the plan, not the messages.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe <T> --hold typical --set "voice mail plan=1" --sweep "number vmail messages=0,1,10,20,32,45"

findings.statement: Daytime minutes add to it in stages once they rise above about 204 minutes ...: going from 0 minutes to 271 minutes moves it from about 2% to about 21%.
findings.check: probe the whole model for the typical customer at 0 and 271 day minutes (charge moved along)
findings.evidence: C107 is a part-scope claim (highDayUsageHinges only). In the block on 'Daytime use and service calls' a reader takes it as the model's prediction: the whole model gives 16.3% at 0 minutes (the light-user service hinge is on) and 50.0% at 271 minutes, with the bill cascade adding +0.76. The threshold (about 204 minutes) and direction hold; the risk numbers are this piece only and should say so. The same applies, less sharply, to the C115 sentence in this block.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe <T> --hold typical --set "total day minutes=271" --set "total day charge=46.07"
uv run python -m explaneat verify probe <T> --hold typical --set "total day minutes=0" --set "total day charge=0"

findings.statement: more voice-mail messages raise it steadily from about 2% to about 2% (annotation adds: flattening out near the bottom because the predicted chance cannot go much lower)
findings.check: read C144 (2.26% -> 2.44%); technical self-probe of the part
findings.evidence: true but says nothing ('2% to 2%'); the saturation clause does not apply at 2%. The readdown hypothesis also picks voice-mail messages as the chain's driver, while the larger movement is from service calls and the international plan (part contribution -0.028 at 1 call to +0.180 at 7 calls, against +0.095 over 0-50 messages, per the stored self-probe).

findings.statement: a higher daytime charge holds it back, more for light daytime users
findings.evidence: garbled: the brake works only while the charge is low (up to about 31 US dollars at 3 calls); 'holds it back more for light users' reads as the opposite of the mechanism (light users get the higher service-call risk). The service-call part of the revision (about 2% to 13% at 4 calls, from about 3 calls) holds.
